samples.summary: Self-removal ("leave workspace") leaves the page in a broken error state
samples.evidence: The diff deliberately keeps the trash button on the viewer's own row (line 325-326: `member.role !== "owner" && (isOwner || member.user.id === me?.id)`), and the test comments document this as intentional self-removal. `removeMemberMutation.onSuccess` (lines 134-138) only does `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["workspaces", workspaceId] })` and toasts "Member removed". After a successful self-removal the user is no longer a member, so the refetch of `fetchWorkspace(workspaceId)` hits `assertMember` in packages/backend/src/workspace/workspace.service.ts:60 and 403s, flipping the page to the generic "Failed to load workspace." error screen (line 216) instead of navigating the user out to a workspace they still belong to. There is no navigation away and no invalidation of the workspace *list*, so the sidebar/list also keeps the stale workspace. (The button existed before this change, but this change is what promotes it to the sanctioned non-owner action.)

samples.summary: Non-owner test races the `me` query: the length-1 assertion can run before fetchMe resolves
samples.evidence: The test waits only on `screen.getByText("Members")`, which renders as soon as the `workspace` query resolves and is independent of the `me` query. The subsequent synchronous `expect(screen.getAllByLabelText("Remove member")).toHaveLength(1)` depends on `me` having resolved, because the button predicate is `(isOwner || member.user.id === me?.id)` — with `me` still undefined there are zero buttons and `getAllByLabelText` throws. Both queries are seeded with resolved promises so they usually settle together, but the assertion is not synchronized on the value it actually depends on, making the test order-dependent/flaky. Wrapping it in `waitFor` would remove the race.

samples.summary: fetchApiKeys mock resolves `undefined`, putting the API-keys query into an error state during the owner test
samples.evidence: `fetchApiKeys: vi.fn()` is never given a resolved value, so in the owner test (where `enabled: !!workspaceId && !!isOwner` is true, workspace-settings.tsx:146) the query function returns `undefined`. React Query rejects a query whose data is `undefined` ("Query data cannot be undefined"), so the API Keys query errors and logs during the run. The assertions still pass because `apiKeys = []` defaults, but the owner test is exercising an error path it does not intend to.

samples.summary: A failing/pending `me` query now silently hides the whole Invites section for a real owner
samples.evidence: `isOwner` (line 87) is `undefined` whenever the `me` query has not resolved or has failed. The Invites section is now wrapped in `{isOwner && (...)}` (line 348) and the invites fetch is gated on `!!isOwner` (line 94). If `fetchMe` fails for any reason short of session expiry, an actual owner sees the page render fine (the `isLoading`/`isError` guards at 191/210 cover only the workspace query) but with Invites silently absent and no indication that anything went wrong. Previously the invites list at least rendered for anyone who could fetch it.
